summary: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy from circa 1920 to 1925 and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences circa 1925–1937.

Boris Vladimirtsov was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Petersburg University (~1904–1908) and under Antoine Meillet (~1908–1909), and held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1919–1931) and the National Library of Russia.

Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery under teachers including Tubten Nyendrak, Khenpo Genam, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and taught Khenpo Chokhyap, Khenpo Dazer, and Jikme Phuntsok.
Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski from circa 1985 to 1993. She served on the faculty at the University of Warsaw circa 1993.

Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned degrees from the University of Virginia (BA, PhD) and Harvard Divinity School (MTS), and also studied at Naropa University. His advisors and teachers included David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He has served as Assistant Director at Boston University and held an affiliation at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Brandon Dotson works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble (~2002–2006) and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich (~2010–2013), holding posts at SOAS (~2007–2010) and Munich (~2010–2018).
Brandon J. Harwood earned a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015), where he studied under advisor Patrick Pranke.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at the University of Calcutta and SOAS (PhD under A. L. Basham), he served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan S. Gillon works in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1980–1985) and served as an associate professor in the Department of Linguistics at McGill University circa 1992.

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, he has taught at Shiga University and Kwansei Gakuin University, and served as Assistant and Associate Professor of Philosophy at Loyola University Maryland.
Brian Bocking is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 1984), where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and was a student of Geshe Wangyal between circa 1968 and 1983.

Brian D. Ruppert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Willis Stoesz (~1982–1986), taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018), and became Professor of Japanese Studies at Bates College circa 2018.

Brian Daizen Victoria is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned degrees from Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple universities, and held faculty posts at the University of Auckland, Antioch University, and the University of Adelaide.

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara (2005) and has served as a Mongolian Language Program Lecturer at UC Berkeley.

Brian Houghton Hodgson worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at Haileybury and Fort William College, he served in the Court of Nepal as Assistant Resident and later as British Resident in Nepal from circa 1833 to 1843.

Brian J. Nichols is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Rice University under Anne C. Klein (attested 2011) and also studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies.

Bridget Allchin worked in archaeology and Indology. Educated at Cape Town and UCL (PhD 1950 under Frederick Zeuner), she was a Fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1976–1994) and served as Secretary and chairman of the Ancient India and Iran Trust.
Brigitte Marschall completed her doctorate at the University of Vienna (~1980–1986) and became an associate university professor (außerordentliche Universitätsprofessorin) there circa 1997.
